title: How quantum computing will break all encryption by 2030

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Quantum computing will break RSA and ECC by 2030—Shor’s algorithm is a proven threat to current encryption protocols.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Quantum computers aren’t scalable yet, and NIST is already standardizing post-quantum cryptography to defend against this threat.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Shor’s algorithm runs in polynomial time on a quantum computer—no classical computer can match that speed for factoring large primes.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance are decades away—current quantum systems are too noisy to execute Shor’s algorithm effectively.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: By 2030, quantum computing won’t break all encryption—post-quantum standards will be in place, and hybrid systems will be the norm.
